answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a thread as the anchor of the cost.
